questions.question: A transport report describes its network in terms of nodes joined by links. In the vertex-and-edge terminology, what are the nodes?
options: The vertices; node is another common name for a vertex
The edges; a node is the connection between two places
Only the vertices at which three or more links meet
Only the start and finish points of a journey

questions.question: An airline network has one vertex per airport and one edge per direct route. A new direct route opens between airports $X$ and $Y$, both already served. What changes in the network?
options: A new vertex for the route is added between $X$ and $Y$
Nothing changes, since $X$ and $Y$ are already vertices of it
One edge $X\text{-}Y$ is added; the vertex set is unchanged
Edges from $X$ and $Y$ to every other airport are added

questions.question: A planner has a road network whose edge values are road lengths in km and wants to know how many lorries per hour the roads can carry. Why can the length values not be reused for this question?
options: They can, after dividing each length by the average driving speed of lorries
Capacities belong to the towns, so only the vertex set needs new values
They can, because a longer road can carry more lorries per hour
Length and capacity are different quantities; capacities must be supplied

questions.question: A network on $A,\dots,F$ has edge lengths $A\text{-}B=4$, $A\text{-}C=2$, $B\text{-}C=1$, $B\text{-}D=5$, $C\text{-}D=8$, $C\text{-}E=10$, $D\text{-}E=2$, $D\text{-}F=6$, $E\text{-}F=3$. In its drawing, $C\text{-}E$ looks shorter than $A\text{-}B$. Which edge is longer?
options: $A\text{-}B$, because its drawn segment is clearly the longer one
Neither; both are single edges, so they are equally long
$C\text{-}E$, with length 10 against 4 for $A\text{-}B$
$B\text{-}C$, which has the largest edge value

questions.question: A student adds a condition to the definition of a network: every vertex must be an end of at least one edge. How does this condition relate to the definition?
options: It is extra; a vertex with no edge is allowed in a network
It is implied, since a vertex with no edge cannot be listed
It is required, since each edge must join two vertices
It is required when the edges carry values, not otherwise
